Sky Metals released its Tallebung study this morning — a project worth roughly A$438m against A$138.8m to build, paying itself back in under seventeen months — and the market answered with a polite 4% shrug. That gap between the news and the reaction is the whole Day plate. It is a 25-cent explorer, so it is a tasting portion, not a main.

It is also the heaviest week of reporting season. Computershare, the top score in tonight's entire 161-name pot at 84/100, reports Wednesday — but it is overbought at RSI 75, so we use a limit order rather than chasing it through the door. For the monthly plate, a confession: our Long slot is 0-for-10, averaging −18.9%, and every failure was the same mistake — buying something that had already run. So tonight it is Charter Hall Retail: supermarket-anchored, 6% yield, 86% tenant retention, sitting a modest 6.6% above its 20-day average. Boring on purpose.

Globally, the pantry is full and almost nothing in it is edible. Atlassian +35%, Doximity +33%, Twilio +25%, Palantir up nearly 40% on the week — a spectacular board, and the model stamped 'too late — wait' on essentially all of it. That is exactly the trade that cost us 22–34% in August. So there is no Day pick, and we are not dressing that up. What survived is quietly excellent: Spectrum Brands earned US$2.79 against a US$1.47 estimate, raised guidance, and has barely moved off its 20-day average. A beat that size which has not yet been paid for is the drift we hunt. Lockheed takes the monthly slot at 53/100 — a 'watch', not a 'buy', so half a portion, honestly labelled.

Watch two things this week: the RBA on Tuesday (a hold is priced — the statement is the event) and US CPI on Wednesday. And ignore Treasury Wine's cheerful 3% bounce; its US write-downs have climbed past $1.2bn. The model scored it 46 and declined. So do we.

geo.body: Crude surged more than 20% through July and has kept a geopolitical premium since: US–Iran tension, Houthi activity in the Red Sea and Saudi retaliation against Iran-aligned forces all threaten the same maritime chokepoints. The counterweight is real though — producers are restoring output and most forecasters still expect supply growth to outpace demand into next year. So: a floor under energy names, not a launchpad.

Rate-sensitive REITs and the banks carry the read-through, which matters directly for tonight's CQR Long pick.

topNews.headline: Sky Metals' Tallebung PFS confirms a low-cost, high-margin tin-tungsten project
topNews.why: Pre-tax NPV(8%) of about A$438m against A$138.8m of build cost, a 69% IRR and payback inside 17 months. At spot prices the study runs to a ~A$1.0bn NPV and 130% IRR. The shares are only up 4% — the market has not finished reading it. This is tonight's Day pick.

topNews.headline: Tabcorp to acquire betting-tech business BetMakers for $267m
topNews.why: A cash takeover at a large premium — BetMakers jumped about 35%. The takeout price now effectively caps it, so the trade is over for new money; Tabcorp (+3%) is the side still worth watching.

topNews.headline: Westpac mortgage applications plunge 20% after budget and rate rises
topNews.why: Down about 5.9% on the day. This is a read-through for the whole banking sector, not just Westpac — falling loan applications point to slower credit growth across the majors. Our sector card has banks marked as rolling over.

topNews.headline: Arena REIT postpones FY26 result as Edge Early Learning seeks rent relief
topNews.why: Down about 15%. A major tenant asking for rent relief AND the result being delayed is a double warning — childcare-property income is not as locked-in as REIT investors assumed. Worth noting alongside our CQR Long pick: CQR is supermarket-anchored with 86% specialty retention, a genuinely different tenant risk.

topNews.headline: Corporate Travel Management extends key UK Ministry of Defence contract
topNews.why: A £28m government contract extension — recurring, defensive revenue from a counterparty that does not default. Scored 59/100 (Buy) tonight, so it made the pot but not the menu.

topNews.headline: Treasury Wine Estates' US write-downs soar above $1.2bn
topNews.why: Read this one carefully — the shares rose about 3% because FY26 earnings guidance beat, but the US write-down is far larger than first reported. Our model scored it just 46/100 (Watch) and did not serve it. A guidance beat sitting on top of a $1.2bn impairment is not the clean result the price move suggests.

topNews.headline: Spectrum Brands' Q3 earnings beat, Home & Garden unit sales up 19% year-on-year
topNews.why: Adjusted EPS of US$2.79 against a US$1.47 consensus, sales up 7.7%, and FY26 guidance raised — yet the stock sits barely above its 20-day average. That gap between the size of the beat and the size of the move is tonight's US Week pick.

topNews.headline: Pentagon presses defence contractors to ramp up weapons production
topNews.why: A direct volume signal for the primes rather than a vague budget headline. Combined with European rearmament and an active Middle East conflict, it is the basis for tonight's US Long pick — though the model only rates Lockheed a 53/100 Watch, so we are sizing it small.

topNews.headline: RBA decides Tuesday 2:30pm AEST — a hold at 4.35% is near-universally expected
topNews.why: All four major banks and all 37 economists in a Reuters poll expect no change, so the decision itself should not move much. The statement is what matters: whether Governor Bullock closes the tightening chapter or keeps hike risk alive. That distinction drives the AUD, the banks and every rate-sensitive REIT — including our CQR Long pick.

topNews.headline: Oil holds a geopolitical risk premium after a 20%+ July surge; copper at record highs
topNews.why: US-Iran tension, Houthi activity in the Red Sea and Saudi retaliation are keeping a floor under crude, while copper is squeezed on supply. Good for energy and copper names (Woodside, Santos, Sandfire, South32 all scored Buy or better tonight), bad for anyone paying the fuel bill. The medium-term counterweight is that producers are restoring output.

chefByMkt.au:
Chef's note — Australia. Tonight the kitchen found something it has genuinely never served before: tin. Sky Metals dropped its Tallebung study this morning — a project worth roughly A$438m against A$138.8m to build it, paying itself back in under seventeen months — and the market has so far responded with a polite 4% shrug. That gap between the news and the reaction is the entire Day plate. It is a 25-cent explorer, so it is a tasting portion, not a main.

Meanwhile it is the heaviest week of reporting season. Computershare — the top score in tonight's entire 161-name pot at 84/100 — reports Wednesday. It is also overbought at RSI 75, so we are using a limit order like adults, not chasing it through the door.

For the monthly plate, a confession: our Long slot is 0-for-10, averaging −18.9%. Every single failure was the same mistake — buying something that had already run. So tonight it is Charter Hall Retail: supermarket-anchored, 6% yield, 86% tenant retention, and sitting a modest 6.6% above its 20-day average. Boring on purpose.

Also worth your attention: Westpac's mortgage applications fell about 20% and the stock dropped nearly 6% — that is a read on the whole banking sector. And do not be fooled by Treasury Wine's cheerful 3% bounce; its US write-downs have climbed past $1.2bn. The model scored it 46 and declined. So do we.
chefByMkt.us:
Chef's note — Global. Some nights the pantry is full and nothing in it is edible. Atlassian +35%, Doximity +33%, FIGS +27%, Twilio +25%, Palantir up nearly 40% on the week — a spectacular board, and the model stamped 'too late — wait' on essentially all of it. Every one had already sprinted past its 20-day average. That is precisely the trade that gave us our worst calls of August, down 22% to 34%. So there is no Day pick, and we are not dressing that up.

What did survive is quietly excellent. Spectrum Brands — pet food, garden gear, shavers — posted adjusted earnings of US$2.79 against a US$1.47 estimate. Nearly double. It raised guidance. And the share price has barely moved off its 20-day average. A beat that size which has not yet been paid for is exactly the drift we hunt.

The monthly plate is deliberately modest. We widened the net across gold, copper, uranium, defence and defensive value — 83 US names in total — and the best of a thin lot was Lockheed Martin at 53/100. That is a 'watch', not a 'buy', and we are labelling it honestly: half a portion, because the Pentagon is pressing contractors to build more weapons and that cycle will not reverse in a month.

Wednesday's US CPI is the real event of the week. Everything reprices off it.
